chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Maqarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Hasan ibn Bandar ibn al-Muthanna al-Tabari narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Maqarri al-Riqqi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Ala' ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: Abu Zakariya narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated from Umara ibn Ghaziya, from Abdullah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, saying:
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: The truly stingy person is the one to whom you are mentioned, and he does not send blessings upon me.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a truly stingy person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this concise definition in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, shifting the focus of stinginess (*bukhl*) from material hoarding to spiritual miserliness in bestowing honor upon the Prophet. This interpretation aligns with the Shia emphasis on *Salat* as a continuous act of worship and divine grace, suggesting that withholding blessings is a form of spiritual poverty. The hadith thus elevates the recitation of *Durood* from a mere ritual to a measure of one's gratitude and spiritual wealth.
